title: Fuse locator-weighted rows with inverse LCH transform boundaries
description: Algorithm 4 receive staging and Algorithm 5 evaluator reconstruction multiply each row by a plan-owned locator factor before an inverse LCH transform. The existing unweighted four-source boundary cannot legally be reused because the diagonal fixed multipliers do not commute through the butterflies. Implement and evaluate a backend primitive or planned coarse kernel that applies four independent fixed multipliers while entering the first inverse layers, preserving null/zero handling, tails, source immutability, active-parent factors and exact wire/profile identity.
acceptance_criteria: Direct interpolation and generic decoder oracles match for GF8/GF16 across scalar/SSSE3/AVX2, active parents, virtual/permanent erasures, arbitrary tails and repeated/concurrent plans; ASan/UBSan plus guard/alias tests pass; operation counts prove a full locator scale/copy pass was removed; same-source isolated benchmarks show at least 5 percent credible benefit in each promoted backend/region with no unexplained neighbor regression over 2 percent, otherwise the candidate is rejected and documented; AUTO changes only for qualified deterministic regions.

comments.text: Implementation derivation frozen before coding: weighted inputs ui=live(i)?ai*si:0, then existing inverse radix-four order v1=u1^u0; v0=u0^m01*v1; v3=u3^u2; v2=u2^m23*v3; o2=v2^v0; o3=v3^v1; o0=v0^m02*o2; o1=v1^m02*o3. title: Restore batched multi-buffer XOR ILP in FF8 XOR transforms
description: The isolated ff8xor XorBuffers helper currently calls one whole-buffer XOR at a time, resolving kernel mode and completing each stream before the next. Restore a native two/four-stream static XOR kernel (and wider AVX-512 variant where useful) for encoder chunk accumulation and the decoder formal-derivative sweep, or fuse those XORs into adjacent transform stages. Keep plane buffers contiguous and preserve portable/128-bit/AVX2 tails and alias safety.
acceptance_criteria: Encode, decode, native round-trip, packed equivalence, k=1/r=1, odd counts, 64-byte tails, and forced-backend tests pass; assembly shows interleaved independent XOR streams with no per-buffer mode resolution in the inner batch; modeled passes/bytes and median/best encode/decode timings are compared against the sequential helper; retain only variants that improve a defined region, otherwise document and reject them.
close_reason: Retained measured small-buffer batched XOR ILP, rejected losing regions, added codec/micro/assembly regressions, documented and committed as 992a1ee.

comments.text: Completed in 992a1ee. XorBuffers resolves mode once and groups 4/2/1 independent streams; named portable/SIMD128/AVX2/AVX-512VL/ZMM two/four-stream loops are retained through 1 KiB, while measured-neutral/slower larger interleaving and manual AVX2 unrolling were rejected in favor of sequential vector loops after the hoisted lookup. Tests cover count 0..9, sizes 64..1536, all forced modes/fallbacks, odd tails, source preservation, and per-pair source==destination; full codec round-trip/packed equivalence/k=1/r=1 remain in the 23/23 Release suite. Strict batch census: AVX2 x2/x4 116/188 B, VL 99/159 B, ZMM 99/175 B; loop XORs 2/4, zero calls/spills/table reads/forbidden ops. Five-run micro geometric speedups: x2 64 B 1.355x median/1.367x best, 1 KiB 1.057x/1.046x; x4 64 B 1.793x/1.794x, 1 KiB 1.117x/1.096x. Larger selected path was neutral. Nine alternating frozen-old/new quick repetitions gave packed-normalized median 1.017x encode and 1.014x decode, but shorter repeats crossed 1.0, so no codec-level speedup is claimed. Transposes excluded; allocation/correctness outside timing.

title: Post-experiment-promotion whole-codebase bug hunt and clean repeat
description: After all promoted experiments are dispositioned and integrated, re-audit the entire first-party tree. Concentrate on interactions between promoted kernels, generated schedules, exact-size or alternate-field profiles, dispatcher tables, serialization, optional backends, and mature fallbacks. File and fix each confirmed defect, then repeat from clean source until a complete pass finds no new actionable bug. Rejected/default-off experiments must also be checked for accidental production reachability.
acceptance_criteria: Every promoted experiment passes its independent oracle plus cross-path, profile/wire, build-option and sanitizer regression gates in the integrated tree; default-off and rejected paths cannot affect production dispatch; each finding is tracked and fixed with a regression; an independent repeat after the last fix records zero new actionable bugs.

title: Make allocation-audit tests compatible with full TSan target builds
description: The whole-tree TSan audit found that the full all-target build cannot link two allocation-audit tests: their deliberate global new/delete overrides conflict with compiler-rt TSan new/delete interceptors. Focused production concurrency tests pass, so this is test-infrastructure coverage loss rather than evidence of a codec race. Separate or condition the audit overrides so a TSan build does not fail at link time while preserving allocation assertions in Release and ASan.
acceptance_criteria: A full TSan configure and all-target build succeeds, or CMake explicitly and narrowly omits only the incompatible allocation-audit executables while registering an equivalent TSan-safe coverage path; Release and ASan allocation-audit tests remain enabled and passing; no broad TSan test exclusion is introduced; exact commands and rationale are recorded.
close_reason: Fixed and validated at 522b667: full TSan target graph builds while Release/ASan retain allocation audits.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Integrated commit 522b667 (source 9ce60d9). Root revalidation: Release affected tests 2/2 and backend matrix self-test passed. Source-branch evidence: Clang18 TSan all-target build succeeds with OpenMP; focused concurrency 9/9; no-OpenMP full TSan 65/65; config-specific TSan flags 2/2; GCC13 Release allocation assertions enabled 2/2; Clang ASan+UBSan allocation assertions enabled 2/2. Only incompatible process-wide new/delete audit hooks are disabled under compiler-detected TSan; full test bodies still run and explicitly report not-audited-thread-sanitizer. No production or broad test exclusion.

title: Post-CUDA integration whole-codebase bug hunt and clean repeat
description: After the optional CUDA backend, build gating, host/device scheduling, codecs, tests, documentation, and promotion evidence are complete, conduct a fresh adversarial review of the entire first-party tree rather than only CUDA files. Audit CPU-only builds and tests-off installs as well as CUDA-enabled paths for ABI drift, accidental CUDA linkage, lifetime/stream races, overflow, tails, aliases, fallback behavior, device selection, error propagation, wire identity, and resource cleanup. File and fix every confirmed defect, then repeat the full hunt until one complete pass finds no new actionable bug.
acceptance_criteria: CUDA-disabled configure/build/install/tests prove zero CUDA compiler/runtime/library requirement; available CUDA correctness, sanitizer-equivalent, fault-injection and large-data stress gates pass; CPU scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 and CUDA results remain wire-identical; each finding has a child bug with regression and validated fix; after the last fix an independent full-tree repeat records zero new actionable defects.

title: Avoid GCC builtin collision in sanitizer runtime attestation
description: The new fuzz replay declares and takes the address of __ubsan_handle_type_mismatch_v1 as a weak no-argument function. GCC 13 recognizes that spelling as a builtin with a different signature and fails TSan/strict builds: declaration ambiguates built-in and built-in must be directly called. Clang ASan/UBSan happened to accept it.
acceptance_criteria: Use a portable evidence probe that does not redeclare or take the address of GCC's builtin identifier; Linux GCC and Clang builds compile; sanitized live attestation still reports UBSan runtime true; non-Linux fuzz smoke remains compilable/fail-closed; Release, strict, ASan/UBSan and campaign self-test pass.
close_reason: Fixed by 53dc1ef: Linux ELF UBSan runtime attestation uses a private weak alias mapped to the exact compiler-rt symbol, avoiding GCC's builtin identifier while preserving live evidence. GCC 13 and Clang 18 strict object compilation pass; GCC TSan fuzz replay targets link; Clang ASan/UBSan API and pruned attestations report compile/runtime/core true; campaign self-test passes.

title: Separate portable-ISA audit from sanitizer-instrumented archives
description: The full Clang ASan/UBSan CTest matrix builds libleopard.a with compiler-rt instrumentation. The portable-ISA disassembly test then rejects a sanitizer-inserted LAHF in Leopard2BackendSSSE3.cpp.o even though the clean Release portability audit passes. This mixes mutually incompatible evidence domains and leaves the sanitizer matrix red without identifying a codec memory error.
acceptance_criteria: Detect instrumented builds deterministically and omit or explicitly skip only the production-object ISA scan with a documented rationale; retain portable-ISA negative/self tests where meaningful; clean Release portable audit passes; ASan/UBSan CTest inventory has no false ISA failure; no broad sanitizer exclusion; controlled tests prove both registrations.
close_reason: Implemented in e0cfa2f: sanitizer builds now register the adversarial portable-ISA checker self-test plus a registration invariant instead of scanning compiler-rt-instrumented archives; clean strict Release retains the production archive audit. Independent worker evidence: Clang ASan+UBSan 65/65, clean strict Clang Release 65/65, focused controls 2/2, Visual Studio structural verifier pass. Coordinator rerun build/high-input-asan completed 65/65 in 24.96s, including leopard2_portable_isa_checker_self_test and leopard2_portable_isa_registration.

title: Gate or port Leopard2 lab self-test on non-Linux hosts
description: CMake registers leopard2_lab_self_test on every platform with Python, but its self-test child unconditionally calls os.sched_getaffinity and is required to succeed. Windows Python lacks that API, so native Windows CTest fails even after C++ portability fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Unsupported hosts either omit the Linux affinity/process-evidence self-test with an explicit rationale or execute a controlled portable fail-closed capability test; Linux registration remains and passes; native Windows CTest inventory proves the unsupported test is not run.
close_reason: Fixed by d9477b1: Linux affinity/proc lab and ELF/POSIX fuzz host-tool self-tests are registered only on Linux; portable codec/Python tests remain. Native Linux lab test passed; controlled Generic inventory omitted the lab test while retaining portable self-tests; integrated Release 74/74 passed.

title: Gate ELF sanitizer campaign self-test to supported hosts
description: The strict fuzz campaign self-test unconditionally requires nm and POSIX symlink semantics, but CMake registered it on every host with Python. MSVC/Windows CTest can therefore fail even though strict campaign attestation is documented Linux/ELF-only. Gate registration to supported Linux hosts while leaving ordinary codec fuzz smoke tests independent.
acceptance_criteria: Linux registers and passes leopard2_fuzz_campaign_self_test; a simulated or actual Windows configure does not register the host-tool self-test; ordinary codec fuzz smoke tests remain registered where otherwise supported; documentation and CMake comments state the contract.
close_reason: CMake now registers the strict nm/symlink campaign self-test only on Linux. Linux focused CTest passed campaign plus both fuzz smokes 3/3. A CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Generic configure omitted campaign while retaining ordinary leopard2_fuzz_smoke (59 tests). Independent second audit confirmed the portability fix.

title: Version strengthened fuzz evidence contract as v4
description: The instrumentation-attested campaign added required target_instrumentation fields while retaining leopard2-fuzz-campaign/v3 and audit/v3. Earlier no-attestation v3 manifests already exist and are rejected by the strengthened validator, so reusing the identifier makes one schema name represent incompatible contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest and audit use v4 identifiers everywhere in code/docs/tests; v3 cannot validate as v4; prior artifacts are explicitly regeneration-only; real attested create/run/audit and mutation tests pass.
close_reason: Parallel manifest/audit contract is versioned leopard2-fuzz-campaign/v4 and audit/v4 in code, docs and mutations. Older v3 artifacts are regeneration-only; real integrated v4 60-job audit passed.

title: Clear stale fuzz manifest before failed create
description: create_manifest performs sanitizer/instrumentation preflight before atomically replacing its destination. If a prior manifest exists and the new preflight fails, the stale manifest remains and can be mistaken for the requested campaign. Audit already clears stale output before validation; create needs the same fail-closed publication rule without ever deleting an executable aliased by --output.
acceptance_criteria: Create rejects output paths equal to either target without modifying them; otherwise it removes a stale destination before preflight; every failure leaves no manifest; successful output remains atomic; self-tests cover stale failure and output/executable aliases.
close_reason: 3843db4 clears stale non-executable manifest output before preflight while refusing resolved executable aliases; modeled stale/failure/alias regressions and campaign self-test pass.

title: Investigate tiny GF8 SSSE3 binary-layout performance instability
description: Valid isolated tests-OFF benchmarking of low-rate final reveal fusion found K=8,R=16,64B,max-loss SSSE3 regressed roughly 4-7% across AUTO, tiled, materialized, and an untouched forced-generic path in the same binary, so the change is sensitive to function/link layout rather than fused arithmetic alone. Investigate generated assembly, alignment/link order, code footprint, and whether extending tiny direct repair beyond L=4 provides a stable dispatcher solution. Retain /tmp/leo2_low_reveal_prod64_latin_isolated_20260718_0818, /tmp/leo2_low_reveal_prod_rep_isolated_20260718_0824, and /tmp/leo2_low_reveal_k8_ssse3_modes_20260718_0821 as current-machine evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce with isolated ABBA/Latin trials in production builds, identify or bound the cause, implement only a stable measured remedy, and add deterministic dispatcher/correctness coverage. Promotion requires credible target-cell gain without >2% neighboring regressions; otherwise document a negative result and retain the existing path.

title: Audit OpenMP GF16 encoder synchronization under TSan
description: During Algorithm 4 final-fusion validation, an OpenMP-enabled TSan run reported a likely synchronization/visibility race across consecutive parallel-for regions in pre-existing GF16 IFFT_DIT_Encoder near LeopardFF16.cpp:1147/1150. TSan startup is itself intermittent on this host (FATAL unexpected memory mapping), while the no-OpenMP immutable-plan TSan test passes. Reproduce in a stable TSan environment, distinguish libgomp/runtime false positive from a missing barrier or shared-state race, and fix any confirmed defect without masking diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Exact failing build/test command and report are retained; stable reproduction or documented external-runtime false-positive analysis; any confirmed race has a focused regression and a standards-based fix; OpenMP and no-OpenMP Release correctness plus TSan where runnable pass; GF16 encode/decode performance and legacy bytes do not regress.
notes:
2026-07-18 integrated no-OpenMP GCC TSan rebuild exposed and fixed a separate fuzz attestation compile bug (53dc1ef). After linking, context_backends and encode_concurrency again terminated immediately with ; API also crashed under the same host run. This confirms the known host TSan runtime blocker persists before useful race evidence. Release and Clang ASan/UBSan/LSan gates remain clean; do not treat this as race exoneration.
Correction to the prior note: the immediate runtime text was FATAL ThreadSanitizer unexpected memory mapping for both context_backends and encode_concurrency. The missing phrase in the prior note was a shell-quoting artifact, not a different failure mode.
2026-07-18 stable audit at root HEAD: GCC13 OpenMP+TSan under setarch x86_64 -R reproduced exit66 in GF16 compatibility at consecutive parallel-for descriptor reuse; raw first report SHA256 0a772d9280d54ad7b1d9d3676b7f6e8099ed7236ca6ec07b7980164985736600. New standalone two-loop OpenMP control reproduces the same exit66 descriptor pattern (raw SHA256 eee0a32bf0f017d9dfee3a919181cb1cde3f6fcc79b6ce7b65b799f379d317ef), proving GCC/libgomp missing happens-before visibility independent of Leopard. Source audit confirms every macro is omp parallel for without nowait, stage regions have implicit barriers, and within-region shard ranges are disjoint. Clang18 TSan with its required ignore_noninstrumented_modules=1 passed the minimal control, GF16 20-profile/360-case matrix, 528 concurrent encodes, and API test. OpenMP Release matrix passed identical parity with 1/2/4/8 threads; no-OpenMP Release passed 360 cases plus 528 concurrent encodes. Candidate documentation/probe is in docs/leopard2_openmp_tsan_audit.md and tests/leopard2/openmp_tsan_barrier_probe.cpp. No hot-path barrier/suppression change; keep in_progress for independent review before negative-defect closure.

title: Fuse exact-pruned Algorithm 5 IFFT schedules into syndrome accumulation
description: The initial GF8 mature-transform accumulation checkpoint intentionally materializes exact-mask C1 input schedules before XORing them into the Algorithm 5 syndrome. Extend the immutable pruned executor with a safe accumulating sink/final boundary so irregular later blocks avoid that extra pass in GF8 and GF16.
acceptance_criteria: Exact-mask input schedules with sparse holes, full/prefix fallbacks, T=2, arbitrary requested originals, tails and every production backend match the materialized oracle; tracing proves only eligible later blocks use the accumulating sink; operation counts and pinned measurements justify promotion without neighboring regression, otherwise record a tested negative result.
close_reason: Implemented in 5412674 after independent zero-new-findings review. Exact Algorithm 5 inverse schedules accumulate at the root without materializing the syndrome block for promoted GF8/GF16 backends; Release 74/74 and Clang sanitizer focused 10/10 pass. Pinned 64 KiB gains were GF8 AVX2 6.843%, GF8 SSSE3 7.818%, GF16 AVX2 7.015%; GF16 SSSE3 4.860% was correctly rejected.

title: Reject legacy aligned-allocation size overflow
description: SIMDSafeAllocate computes kAlignmentBytes + size without checking size_t overflow. A hostile or accidentally extreme internal request can wrap to a tiny calloc, return a pointer advertised for SIZE_MAX bytes, and permit out-of-bounds use. Add a pre-addition guard without changing normal alignment/metadata behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test proves SIZE_MAX and the first overflowing size are rejected before allocation; normal aligned allocations remain zero-filled, aligned, writable, and safely freeable; strict Release and ASan/UBSan public-contract tests pass.
notes: Fixed in LeopardCommon.h with a pre-addition SIZE_MAX guard and added public-contract regressions for SIZE_MAX, first-overflowing size, normal alignment, zero-fill, writable tail, and free. Evidence: Release focused build/test 1/1; GCC strict 1/1; Clang strict 1/1; GCC ASan+UBSan 1/1; git diff --check clean.
close_reason: Overflow guard and regression coverage validated across Release, GCC/Clang strict, and ASan/UBSan.

title: Fuse Algorithm 4 final transform with locator reveal and scatter
description: Algorithm 4 currently evaluates the P-wide accumulator, multiplies each requested coordinate by the inverse locator derivative in a separate pass, then Leopard2 gathers/scatters restored originals. Extend exact/prefix final-transform schedules with requested-output sinks that apply the fixed reveal factor and write caller outputs directly when alias/layout/tail rules allow, retaining the current path as fallback.
acceptance_criteria: GF8/GF16 low-profile direct-oracle recovery is exact for sparse/full losses, tails, padded-odd layout and all supported output aliases; scalar/SSSE3/AVX2, pruned/materialized/tiled, Release, ASan/UBSan and concurrent plans pass; counters prove removed reveal/scatter passes in eligible cells; measured deterministic thresholds avoid regressions and unsupported layouts fall back.
notes: Promoted unconditional Algorithm 4 final reveal/scatter fusion in commits 539c856 and 0823642 (review branch originals 7ff4807/2afe182). Exactness: Release 73/73; strict GCC; Clang ASan+UBSan; no-OpenMP TSan API and concurrent immutable-plan schedule after known loader retries; scalar/SSSE3/AVX2; 20,000 random patterns and 40,000 repeated executes (~233k repaired shards). Isolated production tests-OFF results: GF8 AVX2 K64/R192 1KiB sparse/max +3.66/+29.23%, SSSE3 +10.54/+13.27%; AVX2 K17/R33 max-loss +24.17..27.14% GF8 and +21.89..23.33% GF16 over 4KiB-64KiB, sparse generally +1.5..3.2%. A provisional threshold was rejected because it hurt dense cells. Tiny K8/R16 SSSE3 64B whole-binary layout anomaly is separately tracked as .38.4.1. Evidence and invalid-run disposition: docs/leopard2_low_decode_reveal_fusion.md; authoritative /tmp/leo2_low_reveal_prod64_latin_isolated_20260718_0818, /tmp/leo2_low_reveal_prod_rep_isolated_20260718_0824, /tmp/leo2_low_reveal_k8_ssse3_modes_20260718_0821.
close_reason: Exact direct-output fusion promoted and validated; residual tiny binary-layout anomaly split to .38.4.1.

title: Fuse specialized-decode locator scaling with input transform boundaries
description: Algorithm 4 currently multiplies/copies every received coordinate into work in one pass and then runs each block IFFT; Algorithm 5 similarly copies/zeros inputs before block IFFTs and later performs locator scaling as a separate pass on V_T. Implement and evaluate coarse backend boundary kernels that combine copy/known-zero handling and fixed locator multiplication with the first transform layer where algebra permits, without changing active-parent factors or wire/profile identity.
acceptance_criteria: Direct interpolation, generic decoder, small-field and exact-main recovery oracles match for GF8/GF16, virtual/permanent erasures, tails and repeated plans; scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 tests plus ASan/UBSan and guard pages pass; operation/memory counters prove removed full passes; exact-main/current comparisons establish deterministic target regions or document a negative disposition.
close_reason: Completed by d36f109: qualified GF8 receive-boundary fusion promoted with exact-main/current evidence; rejected backends retain deterministic fallback; correctness, strict, sanitizer and full Release gates pass.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Integrated atomically as d36f109. Qualified GF8 SSSE3/AVX2 unpruned Algorithm 5 blocks fuse caller sources into the first two inverse layers; scalar/NEON retain copy-first and all GF16 retains measured copy-first, with materialized GF16 restored to one parent-wide stage. Exact-pruned syndrome sink remains intact. Root combined-tree gates: build clean and focused 12/12 (legacy, exact stage counters, context backends, operation model, field matrix, CUDA optionality, hook isolation and production-linked sparse benchmark). Agent full Release 76/76, strict Clang, ASan/UBSan, mutation 12/12. AVX2 exact counter tuple K240/R16/loss0: fused4=56,copies=16,zeros=16. Pinned immediate-control gains: AVX2 GF8 64KiB 1.200x; SSSE3 4KiB 1.103x and 64KiB 1.096x; scalar/GF16 rejected below 5%. Exact Leopard main one-loss first/reuse 2.680x/2.689x.

title: Re-evaluate fused high-encode input staging and first IFFT layer
description: Both GF8 and GF16 high encoders still perform separate full copy/zero-fill passes before block IFFT. The legacy comment cites an old ~4% micro-result, but Leopard2's planned kernels and current backend isolation require a fresh implementation/evaluation. Add a backend-range form that consumes caller sources/known-zero leaves into the first fused layer where profitable, including partial final blocks and tails.
acceptance_criteria: Independent exact-main parity/digest oracle passes GF8/GF16 scalar and every qualified SIMD backend; shortened and partial-block inputs do not read null/out-of-range sources; counters demonstrate removed copy/zero passes; Release, ASan/UBSan, aliases and guard tests pass; setup and execution timing gives a promote/reject disposition with deterministic dispatch if retained.
notes:
Current candidate feeds every complete four-shard caller-source group directly through the first two inverse layers using the immutable context backend; only a 1-3-shard ragged group is copied. Exact counters: K32/R16 invokes 8 out-of-place groups/0 copies; K33/R16 invokes 8/1 in both GF8/GF16. Validation on current source: focused Release 13/13, full Release 73/73, strict GCC 8/8, strict Clang 8/8, Clang ASan+UBSan 8/8, no-OpenMP GCC TSan under setarch -R 4/4. Direct generator oracle, legacy goldens, arbitrary tails, source immutability and selected-context callback routing pass. Counterbalanced performance and exact-main gate remain running; known-zero suffix initialization remains a separate C1 input-pruning opportunity rather than an unclaimed removal.
2026-07-18 production implementation committed as a1fa5bf. Complete four-shard source groups feed the selected backend's inverse radix-four kernel without the former active-prefix copy; ragged 1-3 rows retain bounded copying. Deterministic GF16 AVX2 legacy-high fallback returns every T>=256 block to copy-first above 16 KiB. Final tests-off ABBA: 56/56 accepted, exact digests; retained GF8 K240/R16 4KiB 1.268x and GF16 K4096/R16 4KiB 1.122x; qualified fallback cells remain within 0.5% of mature path. Exact Leopard-main comparison is running from detached commit a1fa5bf.
close_reason: Implemented at a1fa5bf with direct radix-four caller-source staging, bounded ragged copies, immutable-source/direct-generator tests, backend routing counters and deterministic GF16 AVX2 fallback. Release 73/73, strict GCC/Clang, ASan/UBSan, TSan and tests-off ABBA gates passed. Eight independently isolated exact-main cells verified with exact parity/recovery digests and zero sibling work: GF8 high encode 1.172-1.194x, balanced 1.037x, field inflation 1.023x; remaining GF16 0.894-0.949x gap is retained under parent leopard-79h.38.5. Evidence: .research/leopard2/exact-main-a1fa5bf-cpu4-cells-20260718/.

title: Make byte-heavy transform threading obey context policy
description: The context thread_count currently controls only cross-item batch workers. Existing GF16 and legacy byte-heavy transform stages still use process-global OpenMP teams, so a context configured with thread_count=1 can execute inner work with ambient OMP_NUM_THREADS, nested batch workers can oversubscribe, and callers cannot fully bound execution through the new API. Replace or gate ambient OpenMP with the context/caller executor policy while preserving legacy API behavior and avoiding per-call thread creation.
acceptance_criteria: New API thread_count=1 creates no inner worker activity regardless of ambient OpenMP; larger explicit counts have a documented deterministic budget shared between batch and inner stages without oversubscription; concurrent contexts do not change global OpenMP state; no hot-path thread creation after prewarm; GF8/GF16 correctness, TSan, nested fuzz, 1..available scaling and neighboring performance pass; legacy leo_* behavior remains compatible or its threading change is explicit.

title: Parallelize independent FF8 payload tiles
description: Execute complete preplanned payload-offset tiles across CPU workers so no barrier is required after every butterfly/layer. Coordinate with cache tiling and reuse metadata plans; preserve a low-overhead single-thread path.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic output and full equivalence pass; 1/2/4/8/... thread scaling, affinity, bandwidth saturation, and NUMA placement are reported; packed and ff8xor use identical thread counts; measured thresholds avoid small-input regressions.

title: Prune and lay out generated FF8 code for front-end locality
description: Emit only reachable variants, group functions by measured call order/frequency, tune alignment/sections, and optionally evaluate ICF, LTO, PGO, or BOLT without making those tools build requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Archive/text size and i-cache/front-end counters improve or negative results are recorded; default and optional build recipes are reproducible; correctness and throughput do not regress on unsupported toolchains.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Four-buffer production adds a 417,744-byte GCC / 559,288-byte Clang object with 256 functions. Include direction/lowering/tuple frequency ordering, cold-section placement for rare tuples, and link-time dead specialization pruning in this task; verify the hot 64-tuple subset and function tables remain deterministic and the actual archive inspector still finds the intended production families.

title: Hoist FF8 kernel resolution and prebuild direct transform plans
description: Resolve the SIMD mode and coefficient function choices once per encode/decode or cached schedule instead of atomic ResolveKernelMode and repeated dispatch per whole-buffer operation. Evaluate ISA-homogeneous entry points, tail branches, and vzeroupper transitions.
acceptance_criteria: No atomic load or mode branch remains inside the transform schedule for the selected path; coefficient dispatch is still outside vector loops; forced backend/tail tests pass; 64-byte through 4-KiB benchmarks quantify overhead reduction.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: New integration follow-up: FourBufferMode is currently a process-global atomic developer selector and TryFourBufferButterfly checks mode/kernel/tuple per radix-4 unit. Snapshot lowering and active ISA once per codec call/transform plan, pre-resolve the 64 tuple function pointers, and make configuration per-call or immutable-plan scoped so concurrent experiments cannot change lowering mid-call. Preserve default-disabled C ABI behavior and unavailable-ISA fallback.

title: Generate size-, truncation-, and erasure-specialized FF8 schedules
description: Emit static schedules for padded sizes 2..256 with fixed bounds, zero-input paths, truncation, and common ErrorBitfield patterns, using the measured schedule corpus to avoid general butterflies where inputs are known zero or missing.
acceptance_criteria: All transform sizes and erasure patterns have an exact generic fallback; specialized schedules contain no dynamic gate interpreter; operation counts, text size, small-buffer latency, and weighted end-to-end effects are reported.

title: Support persistent native-plane FF8 pipelines
description: Provide an explicit experimental usage path for applications that retain shards in native plane layout across repeated encode/decode/storage stages, amortizing boundary conversion without changing the existing Leopard APIs or silently changing compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Layout, lifetime, alias, and work-buffer contract are documented and tested; existing APIs are unchanged; repeated-operation benchmarks quantify amortization and compare fairly with packed pipelines.

title: Evaluate AVX-512 BITALG, VBMI, and mask transposes
description: Compare AVX-512VL/ZMM mask extraction, BITALG/VBMI where present, and 256/512-bit packed-plane transpose kernels. Include feature-safe dispatch, small-buffer effects, code size, and frequency behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Every feature combination safely selects or skips; exhaustive transpose equivalence passes; bidirectional same-process benchmarks identify the best width per size; no AVX-512 requirement is added to normal builds.
notes: Retained feature-safe directional ZMM transposes: AVX-512F+BW+BITALG packed-to-plane (64-byte blocks), AVX-512F+BW+VBMI plane-to-packed (512-byte blocks), with Auto AVX2/portable tails and baseline stubs when disabled. Exhaustive CPUID/XCR0 predicates, groups 1..67 canaries, all 4096 full-block one-hot bits, dense values, source preservation, round trips pass. GCC 13.3 Release pinned ABBA versus AVX2: forward 2.37x..2.77x at 512B..64KiB and 2.41x at 1MiB; inverse 1.82x..2.30x and 1.65x at 1MiB. Rejected redundant VL forward and scalar/gather inverse prototypes. Strict assembly: BITALG 321B/66 insns, 8 VPSHUFBITQMB+8 KMOVQ; VBMI 971B/158 insns, 12 VPTERNLOGD+24 VPERMT2B; no calls, vector stack spills, wrong-width refs, or unexpected vector ISA. Validated GCC hostile global ISA flags plus baseline/directional strict census, Clang18 Debug ASan+UBSan, and AVX2/AVX512-off fallback. Required feature flags append after probed negatives to preserve Clang prerequisite closure. Added uniform unsigned-underflow guards to AVX2 entry points. Full CTest previously 29/29 passed; no commit made by subworker.
close_reason: Implemented, measured, documented, and independently validated the retained AVX-512 BITALG/VBMI boundary-transpose paths; acceptance criteria satisfied.

title: Interleave multiple payload offsets to hide FF8 circuit latency
description: Use AVX2's spare registers to process two multiplier offsets concurrently and evaluate wider AVX-512 independent-chunk scheduling. Interleave identical circuit dependencies while keeping loads/stores in bounds and avoiding register spills.
acceptance_criteria: All 256 coefficients and tails pass; no spills across selected specializations; minimum/average/maximum-depth microbenchmarks and end-to-end tests show statistically repeatable gains or a documented rejection.

title: Search algebraically equivalent FFT layer scalings for cheaper constants
description: Insert compensating nonzero scalings on internal transform wires/layers so external Cantor-basis maps stay unchanged while frequently used multiplication constants become cheaper. Optimize globally, including compensation and fused-stage cost, instead of greedily choosing a locally simple constant.
acceptance_criteria: A field/binary-map proof covers every padded size and truncation path; packed/native equivalence remains exact; no standalone compensation pass is introduced; weighted compiled cost and end-to-end timing decide promotion.

title: Generate non-reversible FF8 circuits with temporary CSEs
description: Use spare architectural registers for common XOR subexpressions and linear straight-line programs, especially eight-wire multiplication, two-buffer AVX-512, and tuple kernels. Add liveness-aware register allocation rather than requiring every candidate to be an in-place reversible CNOT network.
acceptance_criteria: Independent map verification passes; allocator proves or assembly confirms no spills; source remains static named-register code; meaningful coefficient/tuple sets improve compiled cycles or the approach is closed with evidence.

title: Build a deterministic cross-stage FF8 map optimizer
description: Compose and simplify scaling, butterfly, derivative, zero propagation, accumulation, and transpose-boundary maps so cancellations and shared expressions across stage boundaries are visible. Partition fused regions under ISA register and code-size limits.
acceptance_criteria: The optimizer is deterministic and independently verifies every combined map; emits static named-register kernels only; uses a measured cost model; chosen partitions reduce weighted end-to-end time or are retained as documented negatives.

title: Fuse FF8 formal derivative with adjacent FFT work
description: Represent the formal derivative as a static binary-linear map and fuse its XORs into the preceding IFFT output or first FFT layers, preferably inside the tiled plan, while retaining truncation and ErrorBitfield semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A separately implemented oracle proves the combined map for every padded size; decode equivalence passes across sparse and maximum losses; memory traffic and decode timing quantify the effect.
close_reason: Implemented, verified, benchmarked, documented, committed, and pushed formal-derivative/top-sentinel FFT boundary fusion; exact oracle and end-to-end equivalence pass, modeled traffic drops by one third for the replaced stages, and clean AVX2/AVX512 measurements retain the always-on optimization.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Read-only algebra audit found a bounded exact candidate: with h=n/2, the decoder's top FFT skew is always sentinel 255. After the left-half derivative A=D(L), replace the top derivative cross, the entire right-half derivative, and the top FFT layer by ascending q: X[q]=A[q]^R[q]; Y[q]=A[q]^XOR_{b:q_b=0} R[q|(1<<b)]. Sources exceed q, so in-place ascending writes are safe. Independent one-hot basis plus 4096 deterministic random 64-bit states passed for n=2..256. Static traffic falls from 6h+1.5*h*log2(h) shard-byte units to 4h+0.5*h*log2(h), saving h*(log2(h)+2); checked benchmark corpus projects 13.84% byte-weighted decode traffic reduction before zero/materialization effects. Eight static source-arity XOR kernels suffice (0..7); no coefficient/GF circuit dispatch or code-size explosion. Awaiting AVX-512 shared-file integration completion before edits.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Implemented and validated fused FF8Xor decode derivative/top-sentinel boundary. Architecture: after IFFT, compute the unchanged derivative on the left half only; direct row kernel maps each right row q to left=A[q] XOR R[q] and right=A[q] XOR XOR of R[q|bit] for zero bits; skip the sentinel FFT layer and resume at distance n/4. Static named-register arity-specialized kernels, one row-arity dispatch outside each payload loop; uint64, SIMD128, AVX2, AVX512VL, and AVX512ZMM. AVX512 XOR3 uses VPTERNLOG imm 0x96. Tracked path materializes deferred zeros at the boundary and resets state fresh before ErrorBitfield resumes. Independent staged oracle exhausts all n=2..256, all one-hot shard states, zero/all-one, deterministic random states, mixed tails/canaries, all forced modes, and end-to-end/truncated/poisoned tracked cases. Static replaced-stage traffic: old=(6h+1.5*h*log2(h))*B, direct=(4h+0.5*h*log2(h))*B, savings=h*(log2(h)+2)*B, excluding unchanged left derivative. Release focused CTests 4/4 pass including production-object assembly inspection; inspector saw YMM/ZMM 227 instructions, 67 vector instructions, 12 VPTERNLOG sites, one pre-payload indirect jump, zero calls/vector stack refs/forbidden field ops. ASan+UBSan Debug with leak detection passes. AVX2+AVX512 compiled out Release passes focused and core FF8Xor; AVX512-off/AVX2-on Release passes both; full Debug passes both. Clean AVX2 paired sequence on CPU25, GCC13.3 Release, transposes excluded, four-buffer disabled, 2 warmups/7 iterations: decode geometric candidate/control=.928589 overall; by size 1K=.952255, 4K=.943239, 64K=.910595, 1M=.909065; tracked=.909829, untracked=.947736; encode noise=.991255; encode-normalized decode=.936781. By k,r: .920966/.950881/.931009/.938200/.927023/.906361 for 8,2 through 128,128. Raw SHA256: candidate-a 634ebf9676d297835800da22b7eaff3a42ae428994cfc0478bc2cb19f6edc650; control-a2 f324eb2c0d864909b0e3a225dc927b8bbfde897a8bef1a3a298938dc0bfa7edd; candidate-b 01540728130a20280dfd674efb994f869eae37e5d1ad7881dade2820602403fe; control-b 9715ed0f282ee430b25427a929f4d7dc6a14a2e02a6a173ea326405a1d6ee325. AVX512 full sequence from root: raw decode by size .9262/.8922/.8827/.8972; encode-normalized .962/.917/.899/.913. No commit made; stable diff ready for independent review.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Landed and pushed in 774bee8 plus documentation 3eb1778. The exact replacement computes the left-half derivative, then combines the cross-half/right-half derivative and sentinel top FFT in ascending static source-arity rows; the remaining FFT resumes at n/4. Release 40/40, focused Debug, ASan+UBSan, portable-only, AVX512-off, direct all-size oracle, poisoned tracked-state, canary-tail, and ErrorBitfield coverage pass. GCC13 YMM/ZMM whole ApplyRow census: 227 instructions, 67 vector, 12 VPTERNLOG XOR3, zero calls/vector-stack/forbidden field ops; AVX2 likewise has no calls/vector-stack refs. Replacement-stage traffic is exactly 2/3 of old derivative+top FFT; complete 80-row decode model geomean is 0.8564749031x. Clean counterbalanced native timings with transposes and four-buffer fusion excluded: AVX2 decode geomean 0.928589x raw / 0.936781x encode-normalized; AVX512 raw by size 0.926238x, 0.892163x, 0.882675x, 0.897237x. Two independent audits were restarted after documentation findings and ended clean. Clang and real MSVC production-object inspection remain unavailable, explicitly documented.

title: Tune AVX-512 tuple circuits, CSE, and register ILP
description: Generate tuple-specialized four-way butterflies and compare spare-register common subexpressions, independent-offset interleaving, YMM32, and ZMM32 schedules. Audit every selected coefficient/tuple specialization under GCC and Clang.
acceptance_criteria: An ISA-aware choice is made per reachable tuple; every variant is verified; machine-readable census covers spills/instructions/code size; retained schedules improve weighted transform time without front-end regression.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Integration checkpoint narrows this task: final-code repeated aggregates show XOR3 best only for 1KiB encode (0.739x disabled time), while XOR2 is better for 4KiB encode and aggregated decode (e.g. 4KiB 0.784/0.901 encode/decode). At 64KiB and 1MiB both lowerings regress encode (XOR2 1.090/1.086; XOR3 1.177/1.136), while XOR2 decode retains small 0.953/0.988 ratios and XOR3 is neutral. Tune per size/direction/tuple rather than promoting XOR3 uniformly. Preserve the new residency barriers and strict all-256 gate: exactly 32 loads, at most32 stores, no non-vmov vector-memory operands, spills, calls, or non-0x96 VPTERNLOG immediates.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Robust immutable-checkpoint policy run on CPU24: bench SHA e556258d1c5d360f68a7afe353130ba895b9bb45c5be2f7f95fdc65ec06135f2; full 104 schedules, --json --abba, 2 warmups and 7 ABBA rounds (14 samples/row), 3 alternating process reps/mode. Candidate/Disabled median time ratios by B: XOR2 encode .706/.808/1.032/1.008 and decode .920/.936/.974/.998 for 1K/4K/64K/1M; XOR3 encode .675/.799/1.090/1.043 and decode .914/.911/.989/.995. Every fused encode schedule at 1K/4K won >2% in every rep; XOR3 decode strong 20/20 at1K and17/20 at4K. XOR3 versus XOR2 itself is generally only 1-4% aggregate and not robust per schedule. Keep default Disabled; tentative host-specific policy only for ZMM, eligible 64-byte planes, precomputed fused_units>0, and B<=4096. Raw /tmp/ff8xor-policy-abba-{d,x2,x3}{0,1,2}.json and .time. Code tuning/CSE/ILP remains open, so do not close this task.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Superseding aggregation clarification for the immutable three-repetition ABBA corpus: take each schedule's median across the three process reps first, then geometrically aggregate schedules. Final candidate/Disabled time ratios are XOR2 encode 0.747/0.820/1.114/1.065 and decode 0.927/0.927/0.978/1.002 at 1K/4K/64K/1M; XOR3 encode 0.727/0.815/1.161/1.102 and decode 0.914/0.906/0.986/0.999. These replace the earlier aggregate-of-repetition figures in the preceding comment. Confidence conclusion is unchanged: small eligible 1K/4K fusion wins, large uncolored encode regresses, XOR3 versus XOR2 is unresolved, default stays Disabled.

title: Optimize native-plane FF8 XOR circuits on CPUs
description: Drive the checked-in experimental FF8 plane-sliced XOR backend from its measured slower baseline toward the packed Leopard backend. Evaluate circuit synthesis, ISA scheduling, transform fusion, memory traffic, layout, dispatch, and parallelism without changing existing leo_encode/leo_decode behavior. Each candidate must be independently correct, benchmarked against the same-process packed backend, and either promoted with evidence or closed as a documented negative result.
acceptance_criteria: All child experiments have reproducible correctness and performance evidence; promoted variants retain portable, 128-bit, and AVX2 fallbacks and safe runtime dispatch; generated hot loops remain static named-register code with no dynamic gate interpreter; packed Leopard remains unchanged; final gate compares the best enabled native and transpose-inclusive configurations against baseline with median/best throughput, ratios, counters, compiler/CPU details, and candid negative results.

title: Make multi-process fuzz campaigns nested-thread safe
description: The post-Algorithm5 sanitizer sweep launched one process per allowed CPU but each test inherited the OpenMP default, creating roughly 800 runnable threads on a 30-CPU cpuset. Add a reproducible fuzz-campaign spec/runner on top of tools/leopard2_lab.py that pins each seed to its assigned CPU/group, defaults nested runtimes to one thread (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, OMP_DYNAMIC=FALSE and analogous relevant library variables), records the effective environment and observed process/thread counts, and fails or warns before evidence is accepted when aggregate thread demand exceeds the manifest CPU allocation. Preserve an explicit opt-in for tests that intentionally use an internal thread team.
acceptance_criteria: Run at least 30 independent ASan+UBSan API and pruned-transform seeds on this 30-CPU cpuset with distinct logged seeds, no cross-job CPU overlap, bounded per-job memory, aggregate runnable threads consistent with the 30 allocated CPUs, resumable per-job output, deterministic merge, and adversarial tests proving an inherited OpenMP default cannot silently oversubscribe. Scale policy must support 128 allowed CPUs.
notes: 2026-07-18 nested-thread-safe lab and sanitizer campaign integrated at 5168dff through 0ea437e. Exact canonical campaign contracts, live runtime samples, staged publication, never-launched evidence, executable identity and synthetic 128-CPU/256-job validation are covered. Integration exposed a parallel-CTest observation flake; 0afa345 holds three probe threads behind an event and eight simultaneous hostile-environment self-tests plus integrated Release 73/73 pass. Keep open until the required 30 API + 30 pruned ASan+UBSan seeds each complete 8192 runs with audit validation.
close_reason: Acceptance completed in build/fuzz-campaign-integrated-72597bf: 30 API plus 30 pruned Clang ASan/UBSan jobs, 8192 iterations each, 60 distinct logged seeds, one pinned CPU/thread per job, memory bounds and live process/affinity/RSS observations, deterministic v4 audit, and 60/60 zero-work resume. Companion LSan v3 exact replay also passed 60/60.

title: Keep test hooks out of the default installed archive
description: CMake currently defines LEO2_ENABLE_TEST_HOOKS on the canonical leopard target whenever LEO2_BUILD_TESTS=ON, which is the default. The same target is installed, so default libleopard.a exports fault-injection/test-control symbols and includes test-only codec branches. Design a clean build graph or safe default so installed/ordinary production archives contain no test hooks while the correctness suite still exercises hook-enabled code. Add symbol/archive/install assertions, tests-off/on consumer checks, and measure whether removing the hot branches affects Leopard1/Leopard2 comparisons. Do not weaken test coverage or silently install a differently configured wire codec.

title: Freeze odd-GF16 and parity-rebuild API interpretations
description: Resolve two literal plan/API ambiguities before closing the gap audit: (1) arbitrary positive application payloads in GF16 use the explicit GF16_PADDED_ODD_V1 layout and pack/unpack helpers, while native physical GF16 shards remain complete even-byte symbols; (2) optional parity rebuild is an explicit leo2_encode call after combining surviving/restored originals, not a duplicate decode/rebuild entry point. Confirm wire identity, error semantics, tests, and documentation; create implementation beads only if this interpretation is rejected.
notes: Decision accepted on 2026-07-18. Native GF16 retains complete even-byte symbol semantics; arbitrary positive application payloads use the explicit versioned LEO2_SHARD_LAYOUT_GF16_PADDED_ODD_V1 wire layout with B+1 physical bytes and pack/unpack helpers. Parity rebuild is explicitly leo2_encode after combining surviving/restored originals, avoiding a duplicate rebuild hot path. Public contract evidence: leopard2.h, docs/leopard2_api.md, docs/leopard2_gf16_tails.md; audit reconciliation in docs/leopard2_plan_gap_audit.md. Validation on current root candidate: ctest -R 'leopard2_(gf16_padded_odd|decode_low_acceptance|decode_high_acceptance|arbitrary_counts_acceptance)$' => 4/4 pass.
close_reason: API interpretations frozen, documented, and validated by 4/4 focused acceptance tests.

title: Keep historical SIMD fault fixture out of production ISA baseline
description: Full Release 69-test graph after 0cdbcd9 fails leopard2_portable_isa: the intentionally -mssse3 historical whole-TU allocation-failure fixture appears in compile_commands and is classified as a baseline production command. Extend the authenticated portable-ISA checker/CMake metadata to recognize this exact diagnostic target as a privileged fixture while still rejecting any raised ISA floor in canonical leopard objects. Add mutation controls for lookalike targets/sources and rerun full graph.
notes: Integrated as 2113a64. Diagnostic-only historical whole-TU SSSE3 fixture is admitted only with a unique marker, exact reviewed target/source/object mapping, exactly one -mssse3 and -mno-avx, and no additional raised ISA/LTO flags. Embedded controls reject lookalikes, wrong or new sources, production leakage, extra SSE4.1, and missing marker. Agent full Release 69/69, GF8-only/GF16-only portable audits, sh -n and diff-check passed. Root independently passed 68/68 plus portable 1/1 after integration. Follow-up 9d67903 keeps the backend selector warning-clean when the diagnostic build intentionally has no separately linked x86 backend; targeted fixture/portable tests 3/3.
close_reason: Portable ISA audit now scopes the diagnostic fixture without weakening production leakage detection; integrated in 2113a64.

title: Reject legacy shard sizes wider than size_t
description: 32-bit audit found legacy leo_encode/leo_decode accept a 64-byte-divisible uint64_t buffer_bytes above SIZE_MAX. C library copies truncate to size_t while transform loops retain uint64_t, allowing partial copy/out-of-bounds behavior. Reject such sizes before pointer access with Leopard_InvalidSize; test a pure address-width validator against an artificial UINT32_MAX bound on 64-bit and live API behavior conditionally on 32-bit.
notes: Fixed in 1962218. Legacy encode/decode reject positive 64-byte-aligned uint64 lengths above SIZE_MAX before pointer access; artificial UINT32_MAX predicate coverage and conditional real-32-bit API assertions added. Old result-string text intentionally retained byte-for-byte. Integrated Release public/field matrix passed 2/2; independent GCC13, reduced fields, and Clang18 ASan+UBSan passed. Actual -m32 build unavailable because host lacks bits/c++config.h multilib/sysroot.
close_reason: Legacy size_t width truncation eliminated in 1962218

title: Validate codec option size before reading trailing fields
description: Fresh ABI audit reproduced a guard-page fault in leo2_codec_create: it reads options->flags to derive algorithm/workspace masks before validating options->struct_size. A deliberately short prefix at a page boundary must return LEO2_INVALID_ARGUMENT without touching flags/reserved/layout. Reorder prefix validation, preserve v1/current/extended ABI behavior, and add Linux guard-page plus portable undersized-prefix regressions.
notes: Fixed in 6187053. leo2_codec_create validates prefix/partial-layout size before flags/reserved access. Integrated guard-page C ABI regression passes; independent GCC13 Release and Clang18 ASan+UBSan passed exact v1/current/partial/extended cases.
close_reason: Guard-page-safe option prefix validation fixed in 6187053

title: Repair and expand forced-backend matrix coverage
description: Sanitizer/fuzz pass found the forced-backend matrix manifest had drifted and aborted before builds, while compiler identity canonicalized clang++ to clang and linked C++ targets with the C driver. Preserve driver spelling, seal the current source manifest, add missing production/init/pruned tests, and separate backend-dependent run-only output from exact stdout comparisons.
notes: Fixed in 0b269c5. Matrix self-test passes. Independent pass on ce059d8 then completed auto/scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 with 39/38/38/38 records and zero mismatches.
close_reason: Fixed and independently exercised in commit 0b269c5

title: Restore deterministic Leopard2 startup-failure caching
description: Manual pass found regression from d121481: EnsureInitialized calls retryable leo_init on every context creation, so concurrent Leopard2 callers after a one-shot startup OOM/KAT fault observe mixed failure/success and cached-followup contracts fail. Restore a process-wide first-attempt result cache for Leopard2 context construction while retaining serialized retry semantics for direct legacy leo_init callers. Ensure StartupQualificationFailure access cannot race a concurrent legacy retry and validate all 9 backend-fault cases plus contention under TSan.
notes: Fixed in 5296ee2. Shared serialized initializer captures qualification detail under the legacy init lock; Leopard2 caches its first mapped result under its own mutex, while direct leo_init remains retryable. Integrated Release backend failure/public/concurrent/legacy-SIMD suite passed 13/13. Independent agent passed all 9 backend OOM/KAT cases and Clang18 TSan mixed 64-thread initialization plus all three default AVX2 failure cases.
close_reason: Deterministic startup-failure cache restored and race-free in 5296ee2

title: Fail safely when legacy SIMD table allocation fails
description: Root manual audit found LeopardFF8/16 InitializeMultiplyTables in LEO_TRY_SSSE3/AVX2 whole-translation-unit builds assigns SIMDSafeAllocate to Multiply128/256LUT and unconditionally fills the table. OOM therefore dereferences NULL during leo_init instead of returning a platform/setup failure. Make table setup return checked status, preserve retry/idempotence under the serialized initializer, add deterministic allocation-failure injection for legacy SIMD variants, and verify no partial publication/leak or change to portable runtime-dispatch builds.
notes: Fixed in 0cdbcd9. Legacy whole-TU SSSE3/AVX2 FF8/FF16 lookup allocation is checked and failure-atomic, propagates Leopard_Platform, supports retry without reallocating completed fields. Dedicated deterministic failure tests pass for FF8-first and FF16-second; focused Release initialization/public API/field matrix 13/13 passed; agent also passed GCC13 Release and Clang18 ASan+UBSan fault cases plus reduced-field matrix.
close_reason: Fixed and validated in commit 0cdbcd9

title: Preserve Release flags in CMake optimization setup
description: Manual audit found PGI and generic GCC/Clang branches assigning CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE from CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG before appending -O3. This can discard caller/toolchain Release flags and leak Debug flags such as -g/-O0 into Release. Append to the existing Release variable instead, preserve explicit user flags and multi/single-config behavior, and add a configure regression inspecting generated compile commands for Debug/Release separation.
close_reason: Commit a6c7c07 appends O3 to existing Release flags in both generic and PGI branches rather than copying Debug flags. The nested configure/compile_commands regression preserves a Release marker, excludes a Debug marker, and source-checks the unavailable PGI branch. Integrated leopard2_release_flag_isolation passes.

title: Add caller executor and allocation-free batch prewarm path
description: The context-owned pool is persistent after first use but lazily creates/grows workers from a batch call, and no caller-executor adapter exists. Add an explicit setup/prewarm/reserve mechanism and/or versioned caller-executor hooks so applications can guarantee no allocation or thread creation in encode/decode batch execution after setup. Preserve deterministic error ordering, immutable concurrent codec/plan semantics, zero dependency default, per-worker scratch ownership, cancellation/lifetime rules and tests for failure/reentrancy.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Periodic API audit independently reproduced the existing lazy-pool contract gap: first multi-item batch Run->EnsureStarted performs four C++ allocations, second call zero. This matches .14.2; preserve repro first_result=0 first_cpp_allocations=4 second_result=0 second_cpp_allocations=0 and reconcile broad no-execution-allocation claims with explicit prewarm/reserve before closure.

title: Document and verify portable runtime-dispatched builds
description: Evaluate PR #26's LEOPARD_PORTABLE_BUILD_TARGET proposal. Avoid a user-supplied whole-library -march option that still produces CPU-specific binaries; retain the baseline archive plus isolated SSSE3/AVX2 runtime dispatch design, verify the archive boundary, and add concise user-facing CMake portability guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Default CMake adds no -march=native or target-raising baseline flag; baseline archive members remain x86-64 SSE2-safe while named SSSE3/AVX2 members are isolated and runtime-qualified; README explains the default, cross-build/toolchain usage, diagnostic backend controls, and why arbitrary -march values are not called portable; portable ISA CTest passes with negative controls.
notes: Completed in 53e67a7 on top of production isolation commit 77c5038. Rejected PR 26 global march override because it produces a single deployment-specific binary and can contaminate code that runs before dispatch. README now documents default portable runtime dispatch, toolchain-based cross compilation, diagnostic-only backend forcing, and the focused ISA audit command. Independent GCC 13.3 Ninja audit verified baseline objects have no target-raising flags, only the named SSSE3 and AVX2 members have their qualified flags, runtime probe checks CPUID OSXSAVE and XCR0, canonical libleopard.a builds, and leopard2_portable_isa passes with negative controls. A deliberately contaminated march=native build was rejected due to leaked shlx.
close_reason: Portable default, runtime ISA isolation, negative controls, and user guidance independently verified in 77c5038 and 53e67a7.

title: Verify and retain in-bounds FFT skew storage
description: Review PR #28's cast-only workaround for Clang crashing on FFTSkew - 1. Reject pointer-cast masking if it preserves one-before-array UB; ensure both GF8/GF16 use a real sentinel-backed storage base, and validate legacy/new transforms under Clang UBSan and differential tests.
acceptance_criteria: No production expression forms a pointer before FFT skew storage; GF8/GF16 logical factors retain byte-identical indexing; Clang UBSan pointer/array checks and representative legacy/new transform tests pass; the disposition records why the cast-only patch is not adopted.
notes: Disposition: reject PR #28 cast expression (ffe_t*)FFTSkew - 1 because it preserves the same one-before-array pointer arithmetic and only perturbs optimizer behavior. The branch already contains the correct storage fix in commit 284c980: both fields allocate FFTSkewStorage[kOrder], define logical FFTSkew as FFTSkewStorage + 1, and pass FFTSkewStorage plus in-bounds offsets. Source audit found no FFTSkew - 1 expression. Validation on 2026-07-17: Clang 18.1.3 RelWithDebInfo with -fsanitize=undefined,pointer-overflow,array-bounds -fno-sanitize-recover=all built all tests; 49 functional CTests passed including active_lch, transform_differential, legacy_golden, random, high/low acceptance, and fuzz smokes. The sole excluded portable_isa test rejects sanitizer-inserted sahf and is not a runtime or UB failure; its negative controls passed. No code mutation was needed.
close_reason: Already fixed correctly by sentinel-backed in-bounds skew storage in 284c980; Clang UBSan pointer/array suite passed all 49 applicable functional tests; cast-only workaround rejected as still undefined behavior.

title: Add explicit and compile-time finite-field selection contracts
description: Evaluate the proposal to force GF8/GF16 and omit unused field implementations. Leopard2 already accepts leo2_field at codec creation; preserve the legacy leo_* ABI, document the existing force semantics, add deterministic compile-time field capabilities, and make unavailable explicit requests fail safely without silently changing a persisted code identity.
acceptance_criteria: LEO2_FIELD_GF8 and LEO2_FIELD_GF16 forcing plus AUTO behavior are documented and tested; default builds retain both fields and all legacy behavior; supported CMake field-pruning options build GF8-only and GF16-only archives, reject both-disabled configuration, and materially omit the disabled implementation; explicit disabled fields return LEO2_UNSUPPORTED; AUTO retains the same build-independent parent-to-field mapping and returns LEO2_UNSUPPORTED rather than silently changing wire identity when its selected field was omitted; codec/context introspection exposes actual capabilities and field; legacy leo_* never silently changes parity in a reduced build; installed consumers are covered; binary-size and representative GF8/GF16 performance evidence inform explicit choice but never CPU-dependent AUTO wire selection.
notes: Implemented in commit 5c83391. Legacy leo_* ABI remains unchanged; Leopard2 already exposes explicit leo2_field at codec construction. Added deterministic LEOPARD_ENABLE_GF8/GF16 options (both default ON, both OFF rejected), manual NO_LEO_HAS_* controls, disabled source/object/symbol omission, compile-time-safe scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 ops/KAT guards, leo2_context_field_mask(), package capability variables, canonical AUTO no-substitution, and focused reduced-build contracts. Evidence: fresh default GCC Release 61/61 CTests; reduced GF8-only and GF16-only focused tests; recursive reduced build/install/find_package consumer/archive member/nm symbol/both-off matrix; Clang 18 reduced fuzzer builds and representative ASan/UBSan inputs; Python 3.12 and 3.13 CMake/VS parser 131/131; independent read-only contract audit ACCEPT. Archive sizes on this host: dual 4,636,948 bytes; GF8-only 3,271,544; GF16-only 3,554,154. Exploratory pinned AVX2 measurements showed GF8 faster for tested K=240,R=16 and K=10,R=4 cells, disproving a universal GF16 speed premise; field performance remains workload/CPU dependent and AUTO stays wire deterministic.
close_reason: Implemented, independently audited, and validated in commit 5c83391 with dual/reduced build, package, symbol, compatibility, sanitizer-fuzzer, and parser evidence.

title: Normalize CMake Leopard library target and archive name
description: The CMake target is currently named libleopard, so default generators emit liblibleopard.a instead of the conventional libleopard.a. Rename the canonical build/export target to leopard, update all internal links/install/package/tests, and preserve a clearly documented compatibility path for existing downstream CMake consumers if practical.
acceptance_criteria: A default static build produces libleopard.a and no liblibleopard.a; the canonical build target is leopard and installed imported target is leopard::leopard; internal tests/benchmarks and CUDA-optional builds pass; install-and-consume coverage verifies the canonical target and any deliberate compatibility alias; no old API or wire behavior changes.
notes: Completed in commit 0a2a666. Canonical target leopard now produces libleopard.a; source alias libleopard and installed interface compatibility target leopard::libleopard forward to leopard::leopard without a second archive. Independent clean build/install/consume audit passed, including both target names and repeated find_package. Full fresh primary CTest passed 59/59; worker CTest passed 56/56; Visual Studio/CMake contract passed 131/131 under Python 3.12 and 3.13. Historical authenticated runner schema migration remains separately tracked by leopard-79h.36.
close_reason: Canonical artifact and target naming implemented and independently validated in 0a2a666.

title: Prevent legacy Beads execution from tracked Git hooks
description: The tracked .beads/hooks shims invoke bare bd. With Beads 0.47 before Beads 1.1 in PATH, pre-commit rewrites the portable issues.jsonl from the wrong database. Add a portable repository-local launcher that selects only Beads 1.x and route every tracked Git hook through it.
acceptance_criteria: All tracked Beads Git hooks invoke only a verified 1.x binary even when a legacy bd is first in PATH; hook tests pass; a 1.x export containing the hook-repair issue survives commit unchanged.
notes: Implemented in 611dee6. Added executable .beads/bd-v1, which rejects legacy Beads and scans all PATH entries plus inactive NVM installs for a verified 1.x binary. All five tracked Git hooks route through it. POSIX sh -n passed; a PATH with 0.47 first selected 1.1.0; an explicit legacy BEADS_BIN was rejected; pre-commit ran successfully; portable export SHA256 194b8004d007029e83f5ee0fb9728a6fff15ed29dc48848969e8a9b56d701c35 survived commit unchanged and includes leopard-3xi and leopard-lq0.
close_reason: Verified 1.x-only launcher and all tracked Git hooks committed at 611dee6; wrong-database export corruption no longer reproduces.

title: Repair Codex hook binary resolution and remove Kimi MCP registration
description: SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks exit 1 because project hook commands resolve the legacy Beads 0.x binary. Pin hook commands to the repository-required Beads 1.x binary, remove the kimi_k3 MCP registration, validate hook events, and preserve a reproducible configuration handoff.
acceptance_criteria: kimi_k3 is absent from active Codex MCP registrations; SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit commands run with Beads 1.x and exit 0; all modified JSON/TOML parses; tracked configuration changes are committed and pushed.

title: Fix VectorXOR non-multiple-of-four count tails
description: VectorXOR and VectorXOR_Threads process complete four-source groups, then advance pointer arrays using (count-4)-(count%4). For every count at least four that is not divisible by four, the scalar tail reprocesses a completed lane and skips the actual final lane(s). Existing production transform call sites currently pass powers of two, so the demonstrated defect is in the generic internal helper contract rather than current wire output. Discovered by the one-shot Claude/Fable review and independently confirmed from the loop algebra and isolated regression.
acceptance_criteria: Both selected-Ops VectorXOR helpers advance by the exact processed multiple of four; serial and threaded tests cover counts 1 through at least 13 and fail on the old implementation; scalar/SSSE3/AVX2 forced-backend matrices, full release CTest, strict warnings, and ASan/UBSan pass; no wire-format or power-of-two hot-path behavior changes.
notes: Landed as 14aed2f. Vector loop now advances by count&~3u and scalar tail handles count&3u. Regression covers serial/threaded counts 1..13 and fails the old implementation. Independent review CLEAN and found no duplicate faulty arithmetic in current HEAD. AUTO full Release CTest 45/45; forced scalar, SSSE3, and AVX2 backend-op tests pass; isolated review branch also passed strict GCC and Clang ASan+UBSan. Current production call sites use power-of-two counts, so wire bytes and established hot paths are unchanged. The originating Claude CLI call explicitly requested Fable max and found the bug, but usage metadata also logged a small internal Haiku call; that provenance limitation does not affect the independently verified fix.
close_reason: VectorXOR serial/threaded tails are correct for all count remainders and pass release, forced-backend, sanitizer, and independent-review gates.

Hypothesis: The full dyadic block plus exact or dense tail stage can reduce padded computation or define a useful separately versioned exact profile.
Implementation plan: Implement the specified staged scalar model/candidate before optimized kernels; preserve distinction between wire-compatible computation and new code identities.
Correctness oracle: Full padded transform for compatible work; independent direct algebra and exhaustive small-field MDS for exact profiles.
Benchmark cells: All GF8 K,R<=256 plus representative GF16, power boundaries, bytes, batch, and reuse.
Promotion threshold: >=10% meaningful-region measured gain, required identity/MDS gates, deterministic dispatcher.
Kill criterion: Dense joins, setup, memory traffic, complexity, or wire mismatch erase the benefit.
Final result: pending.
acceptance_criteria: Implement and verify the q=2^a+d full-block-plus-tail family against the padded parent oracle for every practical d, comparing direct matrix, smaller padded, recursive truncation, and Newton tail handling; sweep byte size, batch, and reuse and generate a deterministic offline choice table; promote only when wire-identical where claimed and credibly >=10% faster in a meaningful region without neighboring regressions, otherwise document the kill result.
notes:
2026-07-16 resume wave: C3 closed in 3485d92 with independently verified evidence. Begin bounded C4 full-block-plus-tail scalar/correctness/cost checkpoint; keep production/CMake untouched until a candidate clears its promotion gate.
Closed checkpoint evidence: commit e640698. Independent reviewer CLEAN. Main-agent reproduction passed self-test; full one-worker deterministic verify exactly matched 65 jobs, 9,672 vectors, 435,714 comparisons, 50,708 exhaustive GF(2^4) MDS subsets, 8,711 wire-distinguishing witnesses, 402 cost geometries, and 38,592 cells; both retained pinned timing artifacts verified. Result is a documented non-promotion: no production or wire-profile change. Parent-compatible prefix-tail C++/SIMD checkpoint remains future work; exact-tail variants require a separately versioned profile.
close_reason: Completed in e640698 with reproducible artifacts and clean independent review; no candidate met the production promotion gate.

title: Experiment C2: truncated dyadic LCH transform preserving parent
description: Hypothesis: A true truncated forward/inverse LCH transform can avoid materializing unused dyadic-parent suffixes while preserving the exact existing parent code. Implement enclosing-power-of-two transforms with exact active input prefix or sparse mask, exact requested output prefix or mask, complete optimized dyadic blocks plus one irregular boundary, and shifted cosets following Coxon. Oracle: full padded parent transform byte-for-byte; no new coordinate profile is permitted in C2. Benchmark every GF8 K,R<=256 priority region plus representative GF16, setup/reuse, memory traffic, tails, and SIMD regularity. Promotion requires >=10% end-to-end gain, exact legacy/profile parity identity, bounded schedule/code footprint, and no neighboring regression; kill if irregular overhead erases traffic savings.
acceptance_criteria: Forward and inverse truncated transforms match the padded parent for exhaustive GF4 and large GF8/GF16 masks/shifts; legacy-compatible parity is byte-identical; setup/execution and memory traffic are separate; sanitizers/backend determinism pass; any exact-code variant is rejected from C2 and assigned a new versioned profile task.

Disposition: advance flat boundary schedules and complete-subtransform descriptors to bounded C++/SIMD work; do not promote Python execution or thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Implement scalar recursive, flat, complete-subtransform hybrid and bounded generated parent-preserving schedules; match an independent direct-polynomial oracle and the full padded parent byte-for-byte for prefix/sparse masks and tails; reproduce retained results, measure schedule/branch/memory cost, document disposition, and leave production promotion/thresholds to later C++/SIMD gates.

title: Experiment V: optional RVV and HIP batch backends
description: Hypothesis: Optional RVV and HIP batch kernels can accelerate large independent-stripe workloads on already-available hardware without affecting CPU release portability. Implement isolated build options, scalar wire-format oracle, explicit transfer/packing accounting, and ordinary-layout boundaries; CUDA work is tracked separately under leopard-79h.19. Oracle: scalar parity/recovery and exhaustive supported tails. Benchmark realistic batch sizes including transfer cost. Promote only >=10% end-to-end wins with maintained toolchains and no default dependency; kill when hardware/toolchain is unavailable or transfer dominates. Final result: pending.
acceptance_criteria: Only when suitable hardware/toolchains are available, isolate optional RVV and HIP batch builds behind default-off options; verify scalar wire-format identity and failure-free CPU-only configuration; report compilation/runtime hardware precisely and benchmark transfer plus realistic batches; unavailable hardware is a documented inconclusive result and cannot block CPU release.

title: Experiment W: serialized code identifiers
description:

Implementation plan: Version profile, field, K,R,parent,padded side,map; malformed/golden tests.
Correctness oracle: Round-trip and fixed golden byte strings.
Benchmark cells: Parse/serialize/fuzz and migration cases.
Promotion threshold: Stable compact format with forward rules.
Kill criterion: Cannot freeze semantics without unresolved profile math.
Final result: pending.
acceptance_criteria: Specify a compact endian-stable serialized identity for version, profile, field, K,R,parent,padded side, coordinate-map version, and bounded algorithm-independent metadata; implement independent encode/decode with canonical golden bytes, malformed/truncation/overflow/unknown-critical-extension tests, forward rules, migration documentation, cross-endian evidence, and sanitizer/fuzz coverage; CPU backend and autotuning never enter identity; freeze publicly only after exact-profile mathematics and storage semantics are settled.
notes:
Checkpoint evidence 5e7b308: isolated v1 big-endian code-identity proposal with 36-byte canonical header, versioned high/low profile, GF8/GF16 representation, K,R,N,padded side,map version, bounded TLVs, fail-closed critical extensions, and three golden vectors. Python reference passed 10 tests covering 3,952 profile/count/field round trips, 4,162 metadata round trips, all truncations/malformed gates, and 20,000 deterministic mutations. It remains experimental pending independent C implementation and public malformed-input sanitizer fuzzing.
Independent C99 implementation added in commit a1f3d5b. Same full matrix passed ASan+UBSan. Remains experimental pending sustained coverage-guided fuzzing, cross-endian/emulated-endian evidence, frozen exact-profile decision, and justified public storage/API contract.

title: Experiment T: bit-sliced and tower-basis arithmetic
description:

title: Experiment U: generated per-size/profile kernels
description:
Hypothesis: Offline specialization removes branch/zero/output-mask overhead.

acceptance_criteria: Generate offline/template/constexpr per-size/profile schedules specializing constants, zeros, output masks, and fusion under an explicit code-size budget; verify every generated kernel against scalar across fields, tails, masks, and backends; measure compile time, binary/I-cache size, and whole-codec performance; promote only credible >=5% target gains with no unexplained >2% neighboring regression.

title: Experiment R: cache-oblivious and transposed layouts
description:
Hypothesis: Alternative traversal reduces cache/TLB/barriers for large transforms.
Implementation plan: Derive recursive, six-step-like, Stockham, transposed LCH schedules.

Benchmark cells: Large shards/transforms, counters, NUMA.
Promotion threshold: >=10% credible region gain.
Kill criterion: Copies or irregularity dominate.

acceptance_criteria: Derive and implement cache-oblivious, six-step-style, Stockham/autosort, and transposed additive-LCH schedules against the scalar/padded oracle; measure copies, cache/TLB, barriers, prefetch, memory and NUMA traffic across sizes/batches; promote per-region only with byte identity, credible whole-codec gains, bounded scratch/code size, and no mechanical reliance on multiplicative FFT identities.

title: Experiment S: memory traffic and storage policy
description:
Hypothesis: Prefetch/store/page/fusion policy can reduce bandwidth cost.

Benchmark cells: Cache-hot/cold, consumer timing, large shards.

acceptance_criteria: Evaluate prefetch, non-temporal stores, write-combining, shared-zero, huge pages, scatter/compact output, in/out-of-place stages, first/last fusion, and practical page policies; verify memory safety, tails, aliasing, byte identity, and immediate-consumer cases; use counters where available and promote only end-to-end wins in a defined region without privileged requirements or cache-harm regressions.

title: Experiment P: incremental parity updates
description:
Hypothesis: Delta updates beat full encode for few changed sources/ranges.
Implementation plan: Compare direct delta mul-add, transform delta, batching.

acceptance_criteria: Implement direct delta multiply-add, transform-domain delta, batched deltas, and full-reencode comparisons for one/few changed sources and byte ranges; require byte-for-byte equality with fresh encode across profiles, fields, tails, overlap rules, and concurrent ownership; map break-even by updates,K,R,bytes,cache; expose a range API only if race-free semantics stay simple and a credible region benefits.

title: Experiment O: linear circuits for tiny codes
description:

acceptance_criteria: For fixed tiny profiles synthesize bounded XOR/affine or fused multi-source networks; exhaustively verify every generated circuit against scalar/direct encoding and recovery and enforce a code-size budget; benchmark complete tiny-code calls including dispatch and packing; promote only profiles with credible end-to-end gains and no public-layout change, otherwise retain generator/results only.

title: Experiment L: offline autotuning
description:
Hypothesis: Deterministic offline tables improve dispatch across regions.
Implementation plan: Build reproducible tuner for algorithm/backend/tile/fusion/thread selection.

acceptance_criteria: Build a reproducible offline tuner for path, profile where caller identity permits, field where mathematically legal, fusion, tile, threads, and backend; emit a compact deterministic versioned table and manifest with seeds/toolchain/hardware; validate on held-out and neighboring cells with no online normal-startup benchmarking and no CPU-dependent wire selection; promote only after correctness gates and no known calibrated-cell loss.

title: Experiment M: checksum-assisted corruption-to-erasure
description:
Hypothesis: External validation can convert known corruptions into fast erasures.
