acceptance_criteria: Prototype an optional external validation callback or batch prevalidation layer that converts caller-identified corrupt shards into erasures without changing RS algebra; test callback errors, partial batches, concurrency, and unauthenticated-data documentation; benchmark checksum cost separately; keep opt-in and promote only with clear, race-free semantics and no erasure-hot-path regression.

title: Experiment J: plan cache and fixed-pattern batching
description:
Hypothesis: Bounded plan reuse reduces setup for recurring erasures.
Implementation plan: Prototype caller hooks and optional bounded concurrent LRU.
Correctness oracle: Fresh plan results and race tests.
Benchmark cells: Hit ratios, contention, plan sizes, threads.
Promotion threshold: >=10% amortized gain at realistic hit rates.
Kill criterion: Contention/memory overhead dominates.
Final result: pending.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate a bounded optional LRU keyed by serialized codec identity plus erasure bitmap, or caller-managed hooks; prove cache hits match fresh immutable plans and test eviction, malformed keys, concurrency, and bounded memory; measure hit/miss overhead, contention, reuse, and batch patterns; promote only if disabled/default behavior stays allocation-transparent and a defined workload credibly benefits.

title: Experiment K: NUMA task graph
description:
Hypothesis: Per-node pools and first touch reduce cross-node traffic.

Benchmark cells: 1..128 threads across NUMA hardware.
Promotion threshold: >=10% aggregate gain on multi-node host.

acceptance_criteria: On suitable multi-node hardware compare global versus per-NUMA pools, stripe versus byte partition, duplicated tables, first-touch scratch, and optional huge pages; validate race freedom and byte identity; measure 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128 threads with affinity and bandwidth/counter evidence, recording allowed CPUs and topology; promote deterministic policies only where they improve aggregate throughput without harming isolated latency; unsupported hardware remains explicitly open.

title: Experiment I: streaming and incremental encode

Hypothesis: Transform-aware accumulation lowers memory and enables progressive input.

title: Experiment D: GF8 field-boundary rescue

title: Experiment E: incremental locator plans
description: Hypothesis: Add/remove/swap locator delta updates using omega_i+omega_j=omega_(i xor j) can reduce plan setup for nearby erasure patterns. Implement O(N) log-locator updates with correct zero/self and derivative-at-erasure handling for punctures, virtual erasures, and dynamic losses. Oracle: fresh FWHT and sparse-direct locator rebuild plus exhaustive GF4 add/remove/swap sequences. Benchmark stream, RAID rebuild, and packet-window patterns across reuse counts. Promote only if setup falls >=10% without execution or contention regression; kill on fragile zero handling or cache/update cost. Final result: pending.
acceptance_criteria: Implement add/remove/swap locator-plan deltas including self/zero, derivative-at-erasure, puncture, and virtual-erasure cases; exhaustively compare every transition in a small field and large random GF8/GF16 streams with full rebuilds; benchmark O(N) delta against FWHT and sparse rebuild for packet windows and RAID patterns; promote only when correct, contention-safe, and credibly faster in a defined reuse region.

title: Experiment A: GFNI affine multiplication
description:
Hypothesis: GFNI affine maps reduce fixed GF8 multiplication cost.
Implementation plan: Empirically derive matrices; exhaust all multipliers/inputs; implement XMM/YMM/ZMM variants.
Correctness oracle: Scalar GF8 and nibble-table outputs.
Benchmark cells: Mul, full transforms, and codecs across shard sizes.
Promotion threshold: >=5% target-regime codec gain with no neighbor regression >2%.
Kill criterion: No end-to-end gain after setup/downclock effects.
Final result: pending.
acceptance_criteria: Empirically derive GFNI affine matrix bit order in Leopard representation and exhaust all 256 multipliers by all 256 inputs for every supported XMM/YMM/ZMM form, including 0/1 and tails; compare affine, nibble, and GF2P8MULB-plus-basis-conversion in complete transforms/codecs across shard sizes with setup/frequency effects; promote only with a credible >=5% target-region end-to-end win, no unexplained >2% neighbor regression, and additional-microarchitecture evidence; otherwise retain the documented negative/inconclusive result.
notes:
Experiment completed in commit 25ed9b4. Exhaustive 65,536 multiplier/input validation passed for XMM/YMM/ZMM affine, GF2P8MULB-isomorphism, and nibble references; 257-byte tails and ASan/UBSan passed. Pinned two-run 9-sample medians show direct GFNI ZMM codec-like chain gains +7.7% at 1 KiB, +23.2% at 4 KiB, +18.5% at 16 KiB, +0.3% at 64 KiB, but fixed-multiply -2.2% at 16 MiB. Disposition: positive/inconclusive production trial; retain isolated, require size-gated whole-codec validation on additional CPUs before promotion. Evidence docs/leopard2_gfni_affine.md and experiments/leopard2/gfni_affine/. Bead remains open because correctness gate leopard-79h.15 is not yet closed.
2026-07-16 readiness normalization: prior checkpoint evidence is preserved, but the claim was released because explicit active blockers remain and no worker is currently executing this bead. Reclaim after its dependency gate opens (or document a deliberately independent subtask).

title: Experiment B: generated butterfly fusion
description:
Hypothesis: Per-size fused 3/4-layer schedules beat uniform fused-2.
Implementation plan: Search radix/fusion schedules offline and inspect spills/code size.
Correctness oracle: Scalar radix-2 transform.
Benchmark cells: All transform sizes, ISAs, cache regimes, full codecs.
Promotion threshold: >=5% credible whole-codec gain within code-size budget.
Kill criterion: Spills/i-cache negate gain.
Final result: pending.
acceptance_criteria: Search radix-2, fused-2/3/4, and mixed generated schedules by transform size and ISA; verify every kernel bit-for-bit against scalar, inspect spills/code size, and benchmark whole codecs across neighboring cells; promote only per-size schedules with statistically credible >=5% target gains, no unexplained >2% neighboring regression, and acceptable instruction-cache footprint; retain negative results.

title: Lift Jerasure evidence runner parallelism cap safely
description: The optional Jerasure bootstrap/correctness runner hard-caps --jobs and --workers at 10 and serializes that limit into provenance, even when 30 or 128 CPUs are allowed. Replace the arbitrary cap with affinity-aware bounded parallelism and an explicit memory/resource model without invalidating or misrepresenting retained v1-v3 evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Current schema remains strict and replayable; a versioned successor derives default jobs/workers from sched_getaffinity (portable fallback) capped at 128, records any lower resource cap and its reason, validates worker identity, passes adversarial mutation/legacy replay/default-optionality gates, and demonstrates identical 128-case correctness using all safely available CPUs on this host.
notes: Paused 2026-07-18 at explicit user direction: Jerasure comparison is end-stage work after the codec algorithms and exact Leopard-main crossovers. Uncommitted resource-plan prototype was discarded; no evidence or production change retained.
